summary: Iteration 109 verification — AI Conversation Mode (Phase 1) works end-to-end on backend + web + mobile. Backend pytest 9/9 PASS (test_iteration109_ai_conversation_mode.py) covering: personal_ai plain-message auto-route creates session + ai_answer + expires_at populated; group @ai turn followed by 'make it shorter' plain msg routes to AI; low-confidence 'thanks team great job everyone' stays a normal chat msg (no ai_answer); /exit-ai and /team commands return {ai_session_ended:true}, do NOT post a chat message, and flip session active->false; POST /api/chats/{id}/ai-session/exit ends session and is idempotent; parent_message_id reply to an ai_answer routes to AI even after the session was ended; explicit @ai regression still works. Additional ad-hoc verification (script-based): human-mention 'priya what do you think about this' ends session with end_reason=human_addressed, ai_routing_decisions doc logged with final_recipient=chat, confidence_score=0.0, routing_reasons=['mentions_human']; POST /api/chats/{id}/ai-session/route with to='chat' returns {routed:'chat'} and clears pending flag; same route endpoint with to='ai' returns {routed:'ai'} AND fires handle_ai_command producing an ai_question+ai_answer pair. WEB (1440x900, sam@funasia.net): 'What is the capital of France?' typed in My AI Assistant with NO @ai got 'Paris' back; [data-testid=ai-conversation-indicator] renders 'Continuing with @ai' + [data-testid=ai-conversation-exit] Exit AI button; 8 [data-testid^=followups-] chips rendered on the two AI answers (5 chips per bubble: Explain further / Make shorter / Create task / Draft email / Compare options); clicking Exit AI hides the indicator and surfaces the toast 'AI conversation ended. Your next message will go to the chat.'. MOBILE (390x844 via Expo web preview, sam@funasia.net): plain 'Explain briefly what is CPU' auto-routed to AI (mobile shows a proper Markdown bulleted answer); [data-testid=ai-conversation-indicator] + [data-testid=ai-conversation-exit] present; 9 [data-testid^=followups-] chips across three AI-answer bubbles; composer placeholder switches to 'Ask a follow-up…'; tapping Exit AI clears the indicator. No blocking issues. Route-choice UI (route-choice-<msgid> / route-ai-<msgid> / route-chat-<msgid>) was NOT observed during the run because in every one of my ambiguous probes the LLM tie-breaker resolved to >=0.75 and routed to AI directly — this matches the main-agent's context note that the pending_ai_route branch is hard to trigger deterministically. Backend endpoint + service code paths for that branch were code-reviewed and are correctly implemented.
action_items: (Nit / code-review only) /app/backend/services/ai_conversation.py:197 — mentions_human() has a Python operator-precedence bug: `if len(first) >= 3 and f' {first} ' in lower or f' @{first} ' in lower:` binds as `(len>=3 AND name-match) OR @handle-match`, so the length guard is bypassed for the `@handle` branch. Wrap the OR in parentheses for correctness (harmless today because AI handles are already filtered in the earlier @-regex block, but it's a bug waiting to bite).

(Nice-to-have) Add a data-testid on the web AI-conversation-indicator toast/message 'AI conversation ended…' so QA can assert exit feedback explicitly (currently the indicator disappearance is the only signal).

(Nice-to-have) The route-choice branch (pending_ai_route) rarely fires because the LLM tie-breaker almost always resolves to >=THRESHOLD_HIGH. If you want deterministic QA coverage of the 'Continue with AI? / Send to chat' chips, expose a debug/backdoor to force the ambiguous branch (e.g. body prefix `!ambiguous` or a workspace flag) — otherwise this UI path is essentially unreachable in tests.
critical_code_review_comments: services/ai_conversation.py:197 — operator-precedence bug in mentions_human(), see action item.

services/ai_conversation.py:308-311 — personal_ai path fires _trigger_ai() but does NOT call start_or_refresh_session, so a personal-AI chat only gets an active session AFTER the AI answer lands (handle_ai_command must be starting the session downstream). Verified: GET /ai-session returns active=true after the first plain message, so this works — but a comment or an explicit session start here would make the invariant obvious and reduce the coupling to ai_runtime's internals.

routes/ai_conversation.py:97-101 — route_ambiguous_message spawns asyncio.create_task(handle_ai_command(...)) but returns before it completes; the client must poll /messages to see the ai_answer. Consistent with the rest of the codebase's fire-and-forget pattern but worth documenting on the endpoint.

routes/chats.py:1309 — /exit-ai and /team short-circuit path returns immediately WITHOUT running the posting-policy check. That's actually correct (the exit command isn't a normal message) — no bug, just calling it out for future auditors.

context_for_next_testing_agent: AI Conversation Mode Phase 1 is fully working. To hit the ambiguous/route-choice UI branch you almost certainly need to either mock/bypass the _llm_refine step in services/ai_conversation.py or feed a message whose heuristic score sits inside [0.45, 0.75) AND whose LLM tie-breaker also lands in that band — practically unreachable via HTTP alone. If you need to test the [data-testid=route-choice-<msgid>] path, either (a) temporarily mock _llm_refine to return None so the raw heuristic score decides, or (b) directly set metadata.pending_ai_route=true on a message via the DB and reload the chat. All other paths (personal_ai auto-route, group follow-up, low-conf stays chat, /exit-ai, /team, POST /ai-session/exit, POST /ai-session/route, reply-to-AI without session, @-human-mention exit) are covered by the pytest file and pass reliably.
